fatal_errors: The proposed 500–700 °C regime is incompatible with the target immersed tribo-corrosion tests conducted in deionized water at 25–100 °C.
The baseline is incorrectly replaced by an unspecified single-phase HEA rather than identically conditioned duplex stainless steel 2205 and the within-alloy 25 °C reference.

Grain-boundary decohesion and interphase galvanic corrosion are not supported as the controlling mechanisms; the target mechanism is temperature-dependent competition between depassivation, repassivation, tribo-layer stability, abrasion, and oxide-layer disruption.
The predicted 2.5-fold degradation increase is unsupported and conflicts with the observed approximately order-of-magnitude lower wear rate of the eutectic HEA relative to DS2205.
The hypothesis misses the nonmonotonic temperature response, with minimum degradation near 50 °C and greater degradation at both 25 and 100 °C.

The proposed comparison cannot distinguish galvanic coupling from grain-boundary decohesion because changing from a multiphase alloy to an unspecified single-phase alloy simultaneously changes composition, phase structure, hardness, passivation, and mechanical properties.
explanation: The response only aligns at the broad level of considering a multiphase HEA under simultaneous wear and corrosion. It does not reconstruct the alloy, thermal-shock treatment, aqueous reciprocating test, alumina counter-body, or DS2205 comparator. Its mechanism is inconsistent with the observed progression from abrasion at 25 °C to stable-film polishing at 50 °C and disrupted oxidative or third-body wear at 100 °C. E1 provides limited general evidence that some multiphase HEA coatings can undergo galvanic corrosion, but it concerns different coating systems and does not establish the mechanism here. E3 concerns grain-boundary behavior in CoCrFeMnNi and explicitly notes no significant segregation under the referenced sliding conditions; it does not validate decohesion in lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1. E2 does not substantively support the proposed mechanism. Although the falsification rule is explicit, measuring only whether the multiphase material degrades more than a compositionally and structurally different single-phase alloy would not causally test either galvanic coupling or boundary decohesion.
